- File: tests/test_verify_integration_fingerprints_post_capture_evolution.py
  Line or code reference: line 337
  Problem: The negative assertion `"FINGERPRINT_POST_CAPTURE_EVOLUTION_FALSE_POSITIVE_V1" not in out` checks the stdout buffer (`out`), but the production code at `scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:1211` emits the marker to stderr via `file=sys.stderr`.
  Why it fails at runtime: The assertion is vacuously true — the marker is never written to stdout, so the check always passes regardless of whether the marker is emitted on stderr. If a future code change accidentally weakens the defense and causes the false-positive marker to be emitted on stderr during a genuine resolver regression, this test would not catch it. The primary guard `rc == 1` still protects against the regression going undetected, but the supplementary assertion provides zero additional safety.

The new test should follow the same pattern to run in all three unit-test allowlists.
  Expected change site: `.github/workflows/mark-stable.yml` (near line 276, where `test_verify_integration_fingerprints_tiers.py` is listed) and `.github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml` (near line 3336, same location)

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- File: scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py
  Line or code reference: lines 1216-1221 (warning message in _evaluate_fp_state)
  Problem: The warning message states "and no [ai-merge-resolve] commit touched the file in that window, so the resolver did not revert it" but the defense in `_is_must_contain_post_capture_evolution_false_positive` only verifies that the single pickaxe-identified commit (the one that removed the captured line) is not an `[ai-merge-resolve]` commit. It does not verify that no resolver commit touched the file at all.
  Why it fails at runtime: An operator investigating a skipped violation would be told "no [ai-merge-resolve] commit touched the file" when in reality a resolver back-merge may have touched a different line in the same file. The defense decision is still correct, but the warning text asserts a broader claim than what was actually checked, which misleads debugging.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- File: scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py
  Line or code reference: lines 601-606 (_is_must_contain_post_capture_evolution_false_positive git log call)
  Problem: The `git log -S<literal> --first-parent` command has no `--max-count=1` limit, causing it to walk the entire first-parent history even though only the newest (first) hit is used.
  Why it fails at runtime: On long-lived integration branches with thousands of commits this adds unnecessary CPU and I/O overhead to every wave-dispatch verification. The defense only ever uses the first (newest) hit, so limiting to 1 result would be correct and more efficient.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- Requirement: The PR description states "Wired into ci.yml" but the consensus found the test should also be wired into mark-stable.yml and test-and-mark-stable.yml where sibling fingerprint tests already exist.
  Expected change site: `.github/workflows/mark-stable.yml` (near line 276) and `.github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml` (near line 3336)
  Evidence of absence: grep for test_verify_integration_fingerprints_post_capture_evolution in those two files returns no matches; only ci.yml contains the entry.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

=== FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===
- File: tests/test_verify_integration_fingerprints_post_capture_evolution.py
  Line or code reference: lines 337-338
  Problem: The assertion `assert "FINGERPRINT_POST_CAPTURE_EVOLUTION_FALSE_POSITIVE_V1" not in out` checks stdout, but the production code at scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:1209-1224 emits the marker to stderr via `file=sys.stderr`.
  Why it fails at runtime: The variable `out` captures stdout, while stderr is captured in `_err` (which is unused in this test). Since the marker is never written to stdout, this assertion is vacuously true and provides no protection. A future regression that accidentally emits the marker during a genuine resolver regression would pass undetected. The correct check should be `assert "FINGERPRINT_POST_CAPTURE_EVOLUTION_FALSE_POSITIVE_V1" not in _err`.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- File: scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py
  Line or code reference: lines 608-612 (inside _is_must_contain_post_capture_evolution_false_positive)
  Problem: The `except Exception:` clause is overly broad and catches `KeyboardInterrupt` and `SystemExit` in addition to expected exceptions.
  Why it fails at runtime: If the process receives an interrupt signal during the `subprocess.run()` call, the signal is suppressed and the function returns `None` (fail-closed) instead of allowing the signal to propagate. This can cause the program to ignore Ctrl+C and other termination signals.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- Requirement: The new regression test `test_verify_integration_fingerprints_post_capture_evolution.py` must be wired into CI in all workflows that run the sibling fingerprint tests.
  Expected change site: `.github/workflows/mark-stable.yml` (near line 276) and `.github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml` (near line 3336), where sibling fingerprint tests `test_verify_integration_fingerprints_tiers.py`, `test_fingerprint_quarantine.py`, and `test_fingerprint_state_selfheal.py` are already listed.
  Evidence of absence: grep shows no matches for `test_verify_integration_fingerprints_post_capture_evolution` in either file. Only `.github/workflows/ci.yml` contains the new test entry. This creates a gap where the test runs in CI but not in the release-gate workflows (mark-stable, test-and-mark-stable).
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM x-ai_grok-4_20 ===
- File: scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py
  Line or code reference: _is_must_contain_post_capture_evolution_false_positive (~lines 601-612, the `git log -S...` invocation and loop)
  Problem: The pickaxe command runs without `--max-count=1` (or equivalent `--count` + early exit). It walks the entire first-parent history of the integration branch on every `must_contain` miss even though only the first (newest) hit is ever used.
  Why it fails at runtime: On long-lived orchestrator integration branches (thousands of commits) this incurs unnecessary CPU/IO on every wave-dispatch verification and on every resolver run that hits a post-capture miss. The project #3042 incident that motivated this change already demonstrated that these verifications are on the hot path for stall recovery. The `break` after the first qualifying hit makes the remainder of the output dead work.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- Requirement: "The new regression test `test_verify_integration_fingerprints_post_capture_evolution.py` is wired into CI."
  Expected change site: `.github/workflows/mark-stable.yml` (in the unit-test allowlist block near the other fingerprint tests) and `.github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml` (same block, currently containing `test_verify_integration_fingerprints_tiers.py`, `test_fingerprint_quarantine.py`, etc.).
  Evidence of absence: The test is present only in `.github/workflows/ci.yml:198`. The two release-gate workflows that also run the fingerprint test suite were not updated; the test will not execute during `test-and-mark-stable` or the stable-promotion path.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM x-ai_grok-4_20 ===
